summary: PBH is a genuinely cash-rich ($258M FY26 operating cash flow, $0 drawn on $200M revolver, ~6x interest coverage on $1.0B of senior notes, NO_GOING_CONCERN, CLEAN_AUDITOR_TENURE) OTC consumer-healthcare brand aggregator whose -44.6% drawdown is NOT a fraud/solvency story but a real category-headwind story (sterile eye care supply constraints driving -22% YoY Eye & Ear Care segment revenue) being honestly disclosed. The two honesty-alpha catches are: (C3) the unnamed '21%-of-revenue privately-owned pharmaceutical manufacturer' supplier dependency persists across FY24/25/26 with no further disclosure of category split, second-source qualification timeline, or contractual contingency — anonymity that protects PBH's optionality on future supplier acquisitions but obscures the strategic vulnerability; and (C7) the FY26 zero-tradename-impairment outcome is internally inconsistent with -22% Eye & Ear Care decline given that TheraTears is one of the top-5 brands by intangible carrying value, and the relationship between the FY25 $12.5M impairment (specific tradename unnamed) and the FY26 zero charge is not reconciled. Three PASS claims (liquidity, eye-care cadence honesty, acquisition disclosure cadence, insider routine), one UNVERIFIABLE (megacap namecheck inflation-suspect is a known CPG-vertical false-positive), and two MODERATE_UNDERDELIVERY (supplier-anonymity and impairment-zero). Composite 0.333 across 6 verifiable claims (4 PASS / 2 MODERATE / 0 SEVERE / 0 RED FLAG / 1 UNVERIFIABLE) — just above the ≤0.30 small-cap loose threshold, so PBH is BORDERLINE — the two MODERATE underdeliveries (anonymous 21% supplier + unreconciled FY26 impairment-zero against -22% segment decline) are real honesty-alpha catches that prevent the name from cleanly entering Strategy A's index, but neither rises to SEVERE or RED FLAG. The trough is real, the disclosure is largely honest, and the buyback is ACCELERATING (11,413 shares bought in March 2026 at ~$60.49 with $92.2M remaining on plan).
